notes: Delete of a stored fact, as replace-0014. w2's claim that keeping 'Warren was killed at Bunker Hill' would re-derive the battle's war from Warren's is encoded as a firm rule (the battle a man fell at belongs to the war he fell in); the repair search then finds that link must go in w2. The side facts that go with the deleted fact (the battle's date, its place in the siege of Boston) are not encoded: dates are fol and no query asks the siege. q0, q1 and q3 are fol. Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30.

fol.notes: As replace-0014 (years as Int, wars an enumeration with other_war, the battle's 1775 date a side fact that goes with the deleted fact, firm 'killed at a battle: dies in its year and its war'). Delete: w1 keeps 'Warren was killed at Bunker Hill' and nothing dates or places the battle; w2 stores Warren's death by date and war and gives the link up, since through the firm rule it would re-derive the battle's war (the DL file's war_rule_back). revwar_span.says: The American Revolutionary War was fought from 1775 to 1783: its battles fall in 1775-1783. (stored)
revwar_span.z3: ForAll(b, Implies(battle_of(b) == revwar, And(1775 <= occurred_in_year(b), occurred_in_year(b) <= 1783)))

saratoga_revwar.says: The Battles of Saratoga were fought in the American Revolutionary War. (stored)

bh_date.says: The Battle of Bunker Hill was fought on 17 June 1775. (stored side fact of the battle)

warren_at_bh.says: Joseph Warren was killed at the Battle of Bunker Hill. (stored)

killed_rule.says: A man killed at a battle dies in the battle's year and in the battle's war.
killed_rule.z3: Implies(killed_at(warren, bunker_hill), And(died_in_year(warren) == occurred_in_year(bunker_hill), killed_in_war(warren) == battle_of(bunker_hill)))

label_corrections.why: 'Same war as Saratoga' is a join through the functional battle_of (bunker_hill : battle_of some (inv(battle_of) value saratoga)); no dates or arithmetic. The DL file already has battle_of.
